public_comment.topic: Thanked the Lincoln family for privately sponsoring a town band concert and a jazz concert this summer after the override ended town-sponsored concerts.

Promoted the senior-center reading buddies program, raised concern about low third/fifth grade reading proficiency tied to the loss of phonics instruction since 1990, and urged that any new state funding go toward reducing elementary class sizes.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, Five Valley Road, six years
public_comment.topic: Criticized years of lack of progress on municipal building projects and urged the select board to task the Municipal Building Design Committee with a holistic plan for all town buildings, citing the still-unadopted master plan as an example of the town's aversion to planning.

Disputed the town's process for Richard Howard's Trust Fund Commission application, alleging the assistant town manager failed to notify or process his paperwork; the town manager disputed the characterization.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Bradley McNamera to Detective, effective July 7, 2026.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Braden Rozer as seasonal cemetery laborer.
Appoint Anthony Niccastro as a regular member of the Zoning Board of Appeals.
Adopt the current IRS standard mileage rate (.725/72.5 cents) as the town's official mileage reimbursement rate, with future IRS rate changes to apply automatically.
Designate the Cable Advisory Committee positions as special municipal employees.
Acquire by eminent domain a temporary easement at 890 Flatill Road for the Flatill Road bridge project, with damages of $600 to the affected owner, authorizing the chair to execute related documents.
Use police officers (rather than a constable) for the August 8 special town election, the September 1 state primary, and the November 3 state election.
Approve and release the executive session minutes of June 16, 2026.
Approve select board minutes from May 13, 2025, May 19, 2026, and June 17, 2025.

budget_items.topic: FY27 state budget — net revenue impact for Lunenburg
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported the legislature passed the FY27 state budget, and based on the conference committee version Lunenburg would net additional revenue across education aid, unrestricted general government aid, veterans/elderly exemptions, state-owned land payments, and increased charter-school assessments.

budget_items.topic: Local earmarks in FY27 state budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The state budget included earmarks for Lunenburg schools' technology upgrades and for the fire department's aging portable radios.

budget_items.topic: FY26 winter Road/Recovery Assistance Program (RAP) funds
budget_items.what_was_said: A fair share supplemental bill funded a statewide winter recovery assistance program split between a formula pool and a hardship pool that Lunenburg did not qualify for; Lunenburg's formula share will offset the town's snow-and-ice deficit.
A camera system installation project funded through the FY2025 capital program will install and replace security cameras at Town Hall, the Ritter Building, Eagle House, and DPW.

The planning director described the cost of a full site plan review, including an engineering plan, for a business making only minor changes, calling the current requirement not business-friendly and part of the reason for a proposed minor site plan provision.

The planning director is working through about 70 outstanding 53G developer review-fee accounts dating back years and refunding unused balances; project review fees typically run in the low thousands depending on scope.
The planning director noted Lunenburg's tax revenue share from commercial and industrial development is below the threshold that keeps a town from being classified a bedroom community.

budget_items.topic: Additional Chapter 70 funding and possible special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed additional state education funding and whether it would restore staff or fund tutoring/professional development; the town manager said reduced classroom sizes were stated by the school committee not to be the intended use regardless of funding.
The board adopted the current IRS standard mileage rate as the town's reimbursement rate for personal vehicle use on town business, with future IRS changes to apply automatically.

budget_items.topic: Eminent domain easement damages, 890 Flatill Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The board took a new temporary easement for the Flatill Road bridge project after the prior easement expired before construction finished, with damages set by an appraisal of diminished property value.
The board arranged to sign an accounts payable warrant, either via DocuSign or in person.

budget_items.topic: Executive session employment agreements (facilities, HR, Council on Aging, DPW, admin staff)
budget_items.what_was_said: A selectman summarized several employment agreements approved in executive session: a vehicle stipend and added vacation for the facilities director, vacation increases for the HR and Council on Aging directors, a wage step increase, stipends and vacation for the DPW director, and a grade step increase for an administrative employee who absorbed IT/communications duties.
Ratification of a brand-new collective bargaining agreement with Teamsters Local 170 was held pending labor counsel's review of discrepancies.

budget_items.topic: Constable vs. police officer for upcoming elections
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed using a constable versus police officers for three upcoming elections, with one member noting the constable would likely be cheaper, but voted to use police for all three.

transfers.description: Year-end line-item transfers requiring a joint vote of the select board and finance committee

decisions.decision: Get Richard Howard's application paperwork confirmed and place his Trust Fund Commission appointment on a future agenda (targeted July 20) with Howard present.
Board open to having the planning director return after the goals workshop to present Habitat for Humanity options for surplus town lots.
Seek a future-agenda vote granting permission to place the Revolutionary War memorial on town property, leaving exact placement on the lower common to be worked out later with DPW/facilities input.
Defer approval of the August 8 special town election warrant to next week pending town counsel's review of new mailing-notice language.
Board members will submit their goals/objectives ideas to the town manager by Tuesday morning ahead of the July 14 goals workshop.
Try to hold a brief joint meeting with the finance committee, likely at the start of the July 14 meeting, to vote on year-end line-item transfers.
Hold off ratifying the new DPW union (Teamsters Local 170) contract until labor counsel resolves discrepancies.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board ratified a police detective promotion and several routine appointments, heard a lengthy planning-director update and a historical society pitch for a Revolutionary War memorial, and got tangled in a dispute over a stalled Trust Fund Commission appointment. It also acted on several money and process items — adopting the IRS mileage rate, taking an eminent-domain easement for the Flatill Road bridge, designating the Cable Advisory Committee as special municipal employees, choosing police over a constable for three upcoming elections, and approving minutes including newly released executive-session employment agreements — while tabling the DPW union contract, the special election warrant, and the trust fund appointment, and deferring a decision on a special town meeting for additional state education funding.
